fieldValues.title: A concept made reachable by a flat discovery-query can still hide unreachable descendants if it has no contains parent into a Part
fieldValues.summary: PR #704 created three orphan concept records (JSON Store, Import tracking, Registry) with no contains parent of their own. Each was already individually reachable via the spec-glossary's flat concept discovery-query (non-descending), which masked the fact that their contains children (15 mechanism records total) were unreachable -- the exclusions file correctly flagged the 15 children, but nothing flagged the 3 parent concepts themselves as suspect, because they read as published.
evidence: check-publication-reachability.mjs's own header comment already documents the general shape of this bug class (a concept reachable via a non-descending surface while its contains descendants sit below a different, descending surface that never got wired up) -- this is a live instance of exactly that shape, not a new defect in the checker.

Tracing srs#709's 15 excluded mechanism-type records via the full contains relation dump found only 3 distinct parent instanceIds (d6e9ffdd, 714cb3f8, d755fb20), each a dead end: no relation anywhere in the corpus names it as a target of a contains edge.

None of the 3 orphan concepts appeared in scripts/publication-reachability-exclusions.json themselves -- only their mechanism children did -- confirming the concepts read as reachable (via the glossary) even while genuinely un-parented in the tree.

The fix in each case was a single missing contains edge from an existing, already-Part-reachable node (a sibling concept or the Part itself) to the orphan concept; no new Part-level concept was needed once the right existing sibling was identified by reading its own description (e.g. Travelling form's description already names a single-file JSON store as one of the forms it covers).
